pages.definition: A form of communication where the speaker says the opposite of what they actually mean, often to be funny, playful, or to express frustration with a situation. In this lesson, we focus on obvious, exaggerated sarcasm meant to bond over a shared annoyance.
visualCues: Eye rolling or exaggerated widening of eyes
Deadpan expression followed by a smile
toneCues: Lower pitch than normal speaking voice
Heavy, exaggerated emphasis on specific adjectives

scenario.context: You and a friend are standing outside a movie theater. It is pouring rain and neither of you has an umbrella.
scenario.description: Your friend looks up at the dark, stormy sky while water drips off their nose.

audioSample.tonalPrompt: Slow, drawn out, heavy emphasis on 'beautiful' and 'perfect', deep pitch drop at the end.

pages.transcript: Wow, just look at this absolutely beautiful weather. It is just perfect for a walk.

appropriateResponse.description: Reciprocate the sarcasm. Since the speaker is joking about the bad situation to lighten the mood, you should join in rather than pointing out the obvious reality.
keyElements: Add to the joke (e.g., mention getting a tan)

scenario.context: You walk into the breakroom at work and see the sink is overflowing with dirty dishes that have been there for days.
scenario.description: Your coworker stands next to you, staring at the mess with a flat expression.

audioSample.tonalPrompt: Fake sophistication, posh accent, feigned admiration.

pages.transcript: I simply love what the team has done with the place. The smell of old coffee really adds a charming rustic vibe.

appropriateResponse.description: The coworker is using sarcasm to bond over a shared annoyance. Respond with candor by playing along with the 'artistic' interpretation of the mess.
keyElements: Do not offer a literal solution immediately

scenario.context: You and your sibling are waiting in a line that hasn't moved for twenty minutes.
scenario.description: Your sibling sighs loudly and leans heavily against the wall.

pages.transcript: Slow down, everyone. This blistering speed is making me dizzy.

appropriateResponse.description: The speaker is using hyperbole (exaggeration) to highlight how slow the line is. The appropriate response is to share in the complaint using similar exaggeration.
keyElements: Agree with the premise that the line is too fast (irony)
